subject: Compatibility lock and network 'quiet window' — Private upgrade coordination
messages:
From: Timothy Shaw <tim.shaw@acmebank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: infrastructure@acmebank.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster upgrade — request for compat lock + quiet window

Monica / team,

We’re lining up our maintenance calendar for the Private deployment upgrade (v4.3 -> v4.4) and want to confirm Redwood’s requirements for a compatibility lock and a network ‘quiet window’ on our side. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood hold version pins for the upgrade cohorts during the window (no auto-rolls)?
- Is there a recommended 3–4 hour quiet window when you want us to stop external traffic and hold BGP changes?
- What exact artifacts do you need prior to the window (schema diffs, certs, drain scripts)?

We’ve attached our current cutover checklist (upgrade-checklist.xlsx) and would like to propose a tentative window: Apr 23 02:00–06:00 UTC. Will that work?

Tim
Timothy Shaw
Sr. Infrastructure Manager, AcmeBank
attachments: upgrade-checklist.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Shaw <tim.shaw@acmebank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster upgrade — request for compat lock + quiet window

Tim — thanks for the heads up and the checklist. We’re aligned with the concept and I want to put a concrete set of controls in place so the execution is predictable on both sides. Proposed plan below; please confirm acceptance or call out blocking items.

Summary (short):
- Compatibility lock: Redwood will pin the control-plane image and model-serving runtime for the AcmeBank fleet during the maintenance window. No automatic auto-upgrades or autoscaler-driven image changes will be applied between T-24 and T+6.
- Quiet window: We recommend a 4-hour quiet window; your proposed Apr 23 02:00–06:00 UTC is acceptable to Redwood ops.
- Canaries & checkpoints: 2-step canary (staged by rack), KV cache invalidation after canary success, traffic re-introduction by route-level weights.
- Primary rollback criteria: any increase in 5xx rate above 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes, KV cache corruption detected, or failed model handshake on >1 node in canary.

Pre-flight deliverables (due EOD Apr 16):
- schema-diff.txt (what changes at the persistence layer) — required
- Signed network drain script and dry-run results — required (we can run in staging)
- Cert rotation plan (if applicable)

Operational roles (Redwood side):
- Runbook owner: Monica Patel (me) — final go/no-go
- Network lead: Karthik Iyer — will coordinate BGP/VIP failover and netops runbook
- Rollback lead: Soojin Lee — will manage unpin and rollback orchestration if triggered

Attachments I’m including from our side: upgrade-checklist.xlsx (audit checklist we’ll use), and a short schema-diff template.

If this looks OK, please reply with an explicit confirmation and the best contact for the netops window at Acme (we’ll need a phone + Slack escalation).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | monica_patel@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 14:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster upgrade — request for compat lock + quiet window

Adding a couple of technical constraints from network/runbook side. TL;DR: the quiet window needs a short pre-quiesce (10–15m) and a post-validity hold (20m) for BGP convergence and health checks. Also we need an executed netops dry-run at least 72h prior.

Notes:
- Pre-quiesce: start a 15-minute drain where we mark VIPs as 'drain' and reduce LT weights to 0 before the hard cut. This ensures in-flight KV pointers are minimal.
- BGP/EVPN: If Acme intends to touch BGP next-hop during the window, we need explicit step-by-step commands and a maintenance AS-path override plan; partial BGP changes mid-window will force an abort.
- Health checks: our probe timeout will be 5s; if probes fail across >2 racks concurrently, we consider it a canary failure.
- Scripts: I’ve attached a minimal network-drain-script.sh (stub) we’ll expect you to validate in your staging.

Operational checklist updates I’ll make: add a netops rollback step that re-advertises the previous routes and forces graceful connection kills to speed unpin.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
NetOps Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: network-drain-script.sh

Tim — thanks for the quick feedback yesterday. This message confirms Redwood’s acceptance of the Apr 23 02:00–06:00 UTC quiet window and the compatibility lock as outlined below. Please confirm by EOD Apr 12 that the following are delivered to this thread: schema-diff.txt, signed netops dry-run results, and a named phone contact for the on-call netops lead at Acme.

Final execution checklist (short):
- T-72h: netops dry-run (deliverable)
- T-24: compatibility lock enforced in Redwood control plane (no image promotions)
- T-1h: pre-quiesce (15m)
- T0: apply upgrade to canary rack 1
- T+20m: validate, KV flush + probe checks
- T+40m: apply to canary rack 2
- T+90m: progressive rollout if canaries pass
- Abort: immediate unpin + route rollback + catalog revert if rollback criteria met

If Acme confirms, we’ll schedule a 30-minute run-through call next week (suggest Apr 19) to walk the exact commands and validate the scripts.

Monica Patel
